subject: Anatomy
summary: The inguinal canal is a passage in the lower abdominal wall that allows structures to cross from the abdomen to the groin. Its anatomy explains common hernias and the spread of infections. Understanding its relations helps diagnose and treat groin pain.

sections.p: The inguinal canal is a tunnel in the lower abdominal wall, 4–5 cm long, that transmits the spermatic cord in males and the round ligament in females. It is a key site for hernias and infection spread.
b: Transmits spermatic cord (male) or round ligament (female)

sections.p: It runs obliquely from the deep inguinal ring (internal) to the superficial ring (external). The floor is the transversalis fascia, the roof is the internal oblique and transversus abdominis aponeuroses.
b: Deep ring: lateral to inferior epigastric vessels

t.b: Identify location of hernia or obstruction; a palpable bulge at the superficial ring indicates a direct or indirect hernia.

sections.p: Anteriorly lies the external oblique aponeurosis; posteriorly the transversalis fascia. The inferior epigastric vessels run medial to the deep ring. The femoral vessels lie below the superficial ring.
b: Inferior epigastric vessels medial to deep ring

sections.p: Arises from the inferior epigastric artery (medial side) and the deep circumflex iliac artery (lateral side).
The ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric, and genital branch of genitofemoral nerves traverse the canal, providing sensory and motor innervation.
Allows passage of the spermatic cord or round ligament, and facilitates the descent of testes during development.
Hernias (direct, indirect, femoral) are the most common pathology. Infections can spread from the abdomen to the groin via the canal.
b: Indirect hernia: lateral to inferior epigastric vessels
Direct hernia: medial to inferior epigastric vessels

t.b: Detects hernia type and size; confirms presence of bowel or omentum.
Expansile impulse at superficial ring indicates hernia; absence suggests other causes.

sections.p: Ask the patient to cough with head turned away; feel for an impulse at the superficial ring. A loud cough with both hands over the canal can reveal a hidden hernia.
b: Use both hands if no impulse on one side

whenToSeekHelp: Acute groin swelling with pain, fever, or inability to pass stool or urine (possible strangulated hernia).

faq.q: What is the difference between direct and indirect hernias?
faq.a: Indirect hernias follow the inguinal canal lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, while direct hernias protrude medial to them through the Hesselbach triangle.

faq.q: Can infections spread through the inguinal canal?
faq.a: Yes, abdominal infections can track along the canal into the groin, potentially causing cellulitis or abscess.

faq.q: Why is the cough test useful?
faq.a: It increases intra-abdominal pressure, making a hernia bulge more prominent and easier to detect.

exam: Explain the anatomical path of the spermatic cord through the inguinal canal.
Differentiate the three types of inguinal hernias and their clinical signs.
Describe the steps of a physical exam to detect an inguinal hernia using the cough test.
